Subject: Packaging bands & rounding behavior for Integrify pilot discount

Alex / team —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Two quick asks so we can finalize the pilot SOW and the pricing appendix:

1) Can you confirm whether you want billing on (A) per-call token granularity with a 1,000-token minimum per call, or (B) conversation-level aggregation where we round up to 1,000-token bands across all calls per day?

2) For the quoted pilot discount, the legal/procurement team asked for a simple example invoice showing how rounding would apply on a small month (low activity). I attached a sample we prepared (Integrify_Pilot_SampleInvoice.xlsx).

To avoid surprises, our default is option (A) — per-call granularity with a 1,000-token floor per request. Option (B) can reduce bill volatility for bursty traffic but introduces a same-day aggregation rule that affects how leftover tokens are banded.

If you prefer (B) we’ll need to lock the aggregation window to 'calendar day (UTC)' in the SOW. If you pick (A) we can keep the current wording and include one-off credit language for pilot months under 500K tokens.

Can you let us know which you prefer by EOD Friday so we can finalize?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Thanks for the clarity. Quick answers from our side: we lean toward aggregation (B) because our QA tooling fires many short calls (often <200 tokens) and per-call minimums make month-to-month costs spike. Two small follow-ups:

• If we go with calendar-day aggregation, how do you handle crossing UTC midnight for a customer whose primary traffic is PST? Does the aggregation window strictly follow UTC?

• Can you show an example where daily aggregation produces a higher invoice than per-call minimums (we want to understand worst-case for budgeting)?

ProcureOps will need the simple invoice example you mentioned. Mira is copied to coordinate procurement items.

Alex —

Yep — aggregation follows the UTC calendar day by default (we noted that on the call but will make it explicit in the SOW if you choose B).

I attached two short text examples (banding_examples.txt) inside the spreadsheet: one shows a low-activity month (aggregation lowers the bill), the other is a pathological case where many small calls in separate UTC days push you into more 1,000-token bands and increase cost vs per-call minimums.

Short answer on worst-case: aggregation can increase cost vs per-call minimums when your traffic is concentrated into short bursts that straddle UTC midnight (e.g., 11:58pm and 12:02am local time). In that scenario the day boundary prevents the two calls from netting against the same day's band.

I also put a simple rule we can offer in the pilot SOW to mitigate that edge case: an 'anti-splinter' credit that detects likely daylight-boundary splits and auto-aggregates calls within a rolling 10-minute local window for billing only (not for SLOs). That keeps billing predictable without changing the platform's UTC-based aggregation.

Will Karthik and Vanessa can you confirm the math examples below before I send to Integrify procurement?

Example A (per-call floor):
• 30 calls @ 200 tokens each = 30 * 1,000 floor = 30,000 tokens billed

Example B (calendar-day aggregation):
• Same 30 calls all within same UTC day = aggregate tokens = 6,000 tokens billed (rounded up to nearest 1,000 => 6,000)

Example C (worst-case split):
• 20 calls at 200 tokens just before UTC midnight + 20 calls at 200 tokens just after UTC midnight => billed as 20,000 + 20,000 = 40,000 under daily banding if each side rounds up independently.

If that looks right I’ll draft the SOW clause and include the sample invoice.

—Laura

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging bands & rounding behavior for Integrify pilot discount

Laura / Vanessa —

Checked the numbers. Minor tweaks: our system actually rounds bands to the nearest 1,000 upward (ceiling) for billing. So Example B should read: aggregate = 6,000 => stays 6,000 (good). Example C: 20*200 = 4,000 => ceiling to 4,000, and the other side 4,000 => total 8,000 (not 40,000). The earlier 20,000 figures assumed 1,000-token floor per call — mixing the two algorithms in the note created confusion.

To be explicit in the SOW wording I propose: 

"Billing algorithm options (pick one):
1) Per-call floor: each request is billed at ceiling(tokens/1,000)*1,000.
2) Daily aggregation: sum(tokens for UTC calendar day) then bill at ceiling(total_tokens/1,000)*1,000.

Anti-splinter credit (pilot only): detect clusters where >80% of calls are within a rolling 10-minute window crossing UTC boundary and merge for billing purposes. Applies once per account per day and capped at 5,000 tokens credit."

If Integrify agrees we can add the anti-splinter paragraph under 'pilot concessions' and set a single monthly cap (e.g., 50,000 tokens) so finance doesn't worry about unbounded credits.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference
